chapter: Opening and the Budweiser Dance Hall
title: Opening: names, spelling of Rene, date and place of recording
summary: Names of those present are recorded, Rene explains his surname spelling, and the date (7 April 1960) and Kingdom Hall location are set; he notes he is a minister.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: Well, first we'd like to get your name down here. All right.
Marjorie Zander. Paul Crawford. Bill Russell.
And Dick Allen. Is that the middle name? No, it's Joseph Rennie. That's all. We just always carried two names. They had a middle one. We wouldn't know nothing about it.
How do you spell Rennie really?

Well, we used to, when we was playing music, we used to put an R-E-N-E. But now I go on to the R-E-N-E. R-E-N-E, R-E-N-E-A. The name, see? Well, the E have the sound of A, but now I use E now instead of A. But the time we used to play, we used the A.

So your original name is with two E's. Yeah, two E's. R-E-N-E-A. Let's see now. We're about to get the date on here too. Today is Thursday, April? The 7th. The 7th in 1960. And we were recording this at the Kingdom Hall. Yeah, that's right. It's the Seventh-day Adventist Church Hall. No Jehovah's Witnesses. Oh, Jehovah's Witnesses. What am I thinking about?
I read the wrong thing. Yeah.
Today being the 7th. Well, you had that on your mind. That's why we're having it tomorrow. Yeah.
Jehovah's Witnesses. And you're now a minister. Minister, yeah.
